payload.name: Extract speaker actions in shared activities
payload.description: When a message describes an activity shared with others (playdates, classes, group events) and states what the user does as well as what others or pets do, extract the user's own action as a distinct fact; do not summarize only the group or others' actions.
content: During extraction, when a message describes a shared activity and explicitly states what the user does (e.g., chats, watches, helps) alongside what others or pets do, include the user's own action in the candidate content as a distinct fact; do not let the candidate capture only the other participants' experience or the group activity.
When the candidate will UPDATE or MERGE an existing memory, ensure the new content preserves the speaker-action detail even if the existing memory already records the shared activity itself.

solves: Extraction candidates for shared activities often keep only what the other participants or pets did, dropping the user's own explicitly stated behavior, so later questions about the user's role fail. This rule applies to any message describing a joint event (playdates, classes, meetups, group outings) where the user states their own action alongside others' actions: candidates must record the user's action as a distinct fact, and updates/merges must preserve it. It does not apply when the message describes only others' actions with no stated user involvement.
